adjudications.why: Solver agreed with IISER's key (Cr, A) but flagged that the key needs Co(II) in [Co(NH3)4Cl2] to be low spin. Real Co(II) ammine complexes are high spin d7 (3 unpaired, 3.87 BM), which ties with Cr(III). Two defensible answers: owner policy 2026-10-29 case 3, key kept, notice, grace. Solution rewritten because the solver's version taught that NH3 makes Co(II) low spin.
adjudications.notice: IISER's key (option A) assumes the cobalt(II) complex is low spin. Real cobalt(II) ammine complexes are high spin, with three unpaired electrons, which would give option C the same moment as option A. In a PYQ Vault mock this question gives everyone its marks.
adjudications.solution:
Find the oxidation state, the d-electron count and the number of unpaired electrons \(n\) in each complex, then use \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\) BM.

| Complex | Metal ion | d count | Unpaired \(n\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_4(OH)_2]}\) | \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) | \(\mathrm{d^3}\) | 3 |
| \(\mathrm{[V(H_2O)_4I_2]^+}\) | \(\mathrm{V^{3+}}\) | \(\mathrm{d^2}\) | 2 |
| \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]}\) | \(\mathrm{Co^{2+}}\) | \(\mathrm{d^7}\) | 1 if low spin, 3 if high spin |
| \(\mathrm{[Fe(NH_3)_4(CN)_2]^+}\) | \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) | \(\mathrm{d^5}\) | 1 (low spin with \(\mathrm{CN^-}\)) |

A \(\mathrm{d^3}\) ion in an octahedral field always has three unpaired electrons in the \(t_{2g}\) set, whatever the ligand, so \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) gives \(\mu = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\) BM.

The key treats the \(\mathrm{d^7}\) cobalt(II) complex as low spin (one unpaired electron, 1.73 BM), which leaves the chromium complex with the highest moment. So IISER's answer is option (A).
